cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: The control plane stores desired state and continuously works to make actual state match it. It exists because Kubernetes is declarative: you say you want three replicas, not how to start them. A cluster is two tiers: control plane and worker nodes.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: kube-apiserver is the single entry point, etcd stores state, kube-scheduler assigns new Pods to nodes, and kube-controller-manager runs controllers that fix differences. They coordinate through the API server, and kubelets on worker nodes actually run containers. The scheduler filters then scores nodes.

questions.q: Does the scheduler start the Pod?
questions.a: No. It writes a binding setting spec.nodeName. The kubelet on that node starts the containers.
You declare the desired state, and the control plane works out and performs the steps to reach it.

questions.q: How do the control-plane components coordinate?
questions.a: All through the API server, which is the only component that talks to etcd.
